messages:
AlexM: Quick postmortem from the 2:30pm pilot — continuous-batcher + KV prefetch spikes caused a soft-oom on a p4d node. Not a hard crash, but heavy eviction and huge tail latency.
Sara: Ugh. Was that the run with the late-bound prefetch enabled? I thought we had a safety budget.
Jun: Yes, late-bound prefetch was on. The problem is prefetch + large prefix KV churn bumped our live footprint beyond the soft headroom during peak batching windows.
Lina: Can you paste the perf counters from that run? Especially kv_cache_evictions/sec and avg_batch_tokens.
AlexM: Quick dump:
```
kv_cache_evictions/sec: 124
avg_batch_tokens: 258
p50_latency(ms): 18
p95_latency(ms): 72
prefetch_ratio: 0.62
kernel_swap_count: 3
```
Mike: Prefetch_ratio 0.62 is high. We should gate prefetch when avg_batch_tokens > token_budget_target or when evictions/sec spikes.
Jun: Agreed. I prototyped a soft-gating heuristic: if kv_evictions/s > 30 OR (avg_batch_tokens > token_budget_target && prefetch_ratio > 0.4) then reduce prefetch by half for the next 10s window.
Sara: That sounds reasonable. How do we compute token_budget_target? Last experiments used 200-300 depending on quantization. We need a dynamic target based on current KV footprint.
Lina: Proposal: token_budget_target := max(128, floor((available_kv_bytes / avg_kv_bytes_per_token))) where available_kv_bytes = kv_capacity * headroom_fraction.
AlexM: Nice. Headroom_fraction could be 0.7 normally, drop to 0.5 under sustained evictions. Add hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping.
Mike: Also consider kernel selection fallback: when KV pressure high, route short/latency-critical requests to a lightweight kernel that disables prefetch and uses smaller batch windows.
Jun: I ran a quick sim. With token_budget_target=220 and prefetch halved on evictions, p95 drops from 72 -> 55 and evictions/sec drops ~60%. Throughput down ~4%.
Sara: Good tradeoff. Need to ensure we don't starve high-throughput customers. Maybe tier-based policy: enterprise always allowed slightly more headroom.
OpsBot: deploy-bot: canary rollout of batch-gating v1 -> eng-runtime-canary cluster started at 1734503300
Lina: Config snippet for canary:
```
batching:
  token_budget_target: dynamic
  token_budget_floor: 128
  headroom_fraction: 0.7
  prefetch:
    enabled: true
    soft_gate:
      evictions_threshold: 30
      prefetch_scaling: 0.5
      cool_down_s: 10
kernel_routing:
  fallback_kernel: lite-prefetch-off
  fallback_thresholds:
    evictions/s: 50
    avg_batch_tokens: 400
```
AlexM: Can we add a lightweight metric for 'prefetch_benefit' to avoid killing prefetch when it actually helps (cache hit lift per token)?
Jun: Yes, compute benefit = (delta_hitrate / delta_tokens_prefetched). If benefit < 0.002, treat as negative and throttle more aggressively.
Mike: One more safety: if kernel_swap_count spikes > 5 in 2m, pause canary and revert prefetch toggles.
Sara: I'll add alerts and a dashboard tile: kv_headroom, evictions/s, prefetch_ratio, prefetch_benefit, avg_batch_tokens, p95_latency.
AlexM: Great. Next steps: Jun flesh out sim run for mixed traffic, Lina push canary config, Ops run canary through 30m soak and report. Thanks :thumbsup:
_reserved_note: No title per agents.md. Thread content is a single string of messages in chronological order as required.
